Every commercial stack drifts toward the same patchwork: a recording tool here, a content platform there, an enablement layer somewhere else, each holding a fragment of the truth. Sellers feel the seams every day. UiPath decided to be done with that. The choice was not another point solution. It was one governed intelligence layer spanning the entire commercial organization.

It started where a seller feels the scatter first: the content itself. One governed home for approved materials now gives UiPath’s sellers a single place where the answers have already been vetted. Product questions come back with citations. Documents surface from across Highspot, Confluence and SharePoint without anyone having to remember which system holds what.

Before the call, the work that used to eat a rep’s morning happens on its own. Workflows research the account, build the point of view, and read risk off CRM data and recorded calls that have flowed into the governed layer, so a rep opens a deal already knowing where it stands. Prep assembles itself rather than being assembled, down to the proof points tied to that customer’s specific pain.

During the call, Scribe, Tribble’s call recorder, works alongside the seller: coaching in the moment, and holding the questions that need a real expert answer rather than a guess. JR Kelly, who leads enablement at UiPath, installed it the night he got access and spent the next day working inside it.

The most telling extension of the platform points outward. UiPath opened a Partner Agent, built on the same governed foundation, to its partner ecosystem, and 350+ partners now have access. Over the last ten months it has answered 5,200+ partner questions spanning product support, general Q and A, pricing, training, customer stories, solution kits and the partner accelerator program.

Create a unified knowledge layer that holds everything the company already knows, and it gets smarter with every project, every call and every question answered, internally and across the partner ecosystem alike. That is what a modern commercial stack looks like when the tools stop competing for attention.

Sprout’s go-to-market engine runs on Salesforce and Highspot, and like most fast-moving revenue organizations, its deal intelligence lives across systems: answers in the CRM, plays in the content library, context in call recordings and spreadsheets, with the reporting people trusted most sitting in Tableau and Redshift, and reps re-assembling deal context by hand.

The conventional fix is a consolidation effort: launch a platform, migrate everything onto it, and retrain the organization around a new system of record. Sprout’s revenue operations team chose differently. They decided to strategically drop Tribble into every deal channel to solve their scattered-knowledge problem.
The people behind workflows like that are Sprout’s operators, the RevOps and sales-ops practitioners who build, govern, and connect the systems their revenue team runs on.
Rather than a broad platform rollout, revenue operations added Tribble to every deal channel and let one workflow prove the benefits. That plan is now part of how the team operates.

Sprout’s operators, the RevOps and sales-ops practitioners who run the revenue stack. They wrote the guide to which Salesforce fields are most reliable and set the data-hygiene discipline: fix the record before you automate on top of it.

Every revenue leader knows the feeling: the number is somewhere. It’s in the CRM, in the finance system, in a spreadsheet someone maintains by hand, in a report that’s three days stale. The data exists. It just doesn’t agree with itself, and by the time it’s reconciled for the board, the moment to act on it has passed.

Lead hygiene that scans the pipeline for leads gone quiet, a weekly opportunity report that lands with every manager Friday at 8am, and board-level revenue forecasting produced continuously by the Brain.
